transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2027-09-29
Start: 15:00 UTC
Duration: 58 minutes
Location: Zoom
Attendees: Sophie (Redwood AE), Diego (Redwood SE), Anika (Redwood Partnerships), Priya (Verdant Head of Partnerships), Liam (Verdant CTO), Samir (Verdant Platform), Jade (Verdant Product)

Auto-summary (auto-gen, may be incomplete):
- Intro + partner motion overview, onramp/go-to-market intent
- Technical constraints: multi-tenant marketplace, billing integration, HSM/KMS, VPC peering, kernel support (NVIDIA A100/p4?), MIG, quantization and perf profiling
- Next steps: share integration spec, terraform module, schedule SE deep dive, pilot scope defined loosely (3 customers, EU/US)

Transcript:
[00:00] Sophie: Hey everyone, thanks for making time. Quick round of intros and then we'll share what Redwood does and hear about Verdant's onramp goals. Um, Priya do you want to kick us off?
[00:14] Priya: Yeah hi all. Thanks, Sophie. We're Verdant Accelerators; we resell and manage GPU capacity to SaaS partners, mostly in EU and NA, and we're looking to streamline a marketplace onramp for inference stacks. We want an easy way to list Redwood-hosted models + ability to run private deployments with our customers.
[00:31] Liam: Hi, I'm Liam, CTO. The two big things for us are orchestration compatibility with our fleet manager and a billing hook so we can surface cost and revenue share. Also we need to know what hardware profiles Redwood supports—like do you have MIG support, and what about AMD/MI100 class cards?
[00:48] Diego: Great context. Quick answer: Redwood's runtime supports a range of backends. We optimize kernels per architecture; we do have MIG-aware scheduling for NVIDIA A100 and A10, and we also run workloads on Ampere-like and some AMD GPUs in partner environments, though there are perf differences. I can share compatibility matrix after.
[01:05] Jade: When you said "private deployments" — are you talking full private control plane or VPC peering model? We need to present correct options to customers.
[01:12] Anika: For partner onramps we usually offer both: a VPC peering option for customers who want network-level isolation, and an on-prem/air-gapped package for larger regulated customers. The private control plane can be provisioned in a partner-managed VPC so you can maintain audit controls.
[01:25] Samir: Cool. On the billing front, how do we integrate? We want line-item granularity per-tenant, per-model. Is there a webhook or metering API?
[01:34] Sophie: Yes — we expose a usage events stream (S3/streaming) and a metering API. Partners can either pull aggregated CSVs or subscribe to event webhooks. We also support marketplace billing integrations (we've done things with cloud marketplaces and reseller flows).
[01:45] Liam: Any examples of revenue share flows or invoicing automation you've done?
[01:49] Sophie: We helped a reseller integrate a rev-share where partner receives monthly settlements; Redwood emits usage reports with cost-basis and partner offset, then legal defines settlement cadence. We can share the template.
[01:58] Priya: Awesome. For our initial pilot we expect three anchor customers — one EU financial, one NA medtech, and one global e‑commerce. Each has different compliance needs. SOC2 is baseline, but the financial customer needs stricter audit logging and potential HSM integration.
[02:15] Diego: HSM/KMS integration is supported — we integrate with AWS KMS, GCP KMS, and customers can bring their own keys. For private deployments we can wire in HSMs; there's some ops complexity but we've done it.
[02:27] Priya: Good. How about data residency? The EU customer won't accept even transient token storage outside region.
[02:33] Diego: We can keep inference confined to specific regions and enforce routing. Our smart routing can ensure requests are pinned to EU capacity and fall back only to compatible EU-hosted variants. I'll note though that certain open model mirrors might not be present in all regions — we can bundle a mirrored model for the pilot.
[02:49] Jade: On the ops side, does Redwood provide a Kubernetes operator or terraform modules so Verdant can automate provisioning for customers?
[02:56] Diego: We expose Terraform modules and a controller; for private deployments we provide a Helm chart and operator snippets. Partners often use our module as a starting point and add their fleet manager hooks. We'll share the repo link after the call.
[03:09] Samir: Great. I want to dig in a bit on perf — we need to understand SLOs per model variant, batching tradeoffs, and cold-start behavior.
[03:18] Diego: Sure. Our runtime supports continuous batching and KV cache sharing. For large models the latency/cost tradeoff is influenced by batch size and sequence length. We typically provide a perf profile per model: p50/p95 token latency at various seq lengths and batch sizes. For cold-starts we have warm pools and can provide burst capacity. I'll put sample perf curves in the doc.
[03:40] Liam: Do you do quantized model variants for cost-savings, and are those output-stable versus float32?
[03:46] Diego: Yes — quantized variants are offered. We run evals and quality gates; in production we recommend running A/Bs against your critical prompts. The Optimize tooling suggests quantization based on workload. Some degredation is possible for specific prompts; we'll provide the eval reports.
[03:59] Priya: One of our legal ask's is around audit logs for partner customers. We need to capture token-level logs, who invoked what, and for how long. Retention windows vary by customer. Is that surfaced?
[04:10] Anika: We capture structured logs and can ship them to partner SIEMs or provide retention policies per deployment. For marketplace listings there's a default retention but partners can request extended retention for an additional fee.
[04:22] Sophie: Quick interactive question — what's your timeline for pilot?
[04:25] Priya: We want to onboard the first customer by late Q4, ideally a soft pilot in early December. So timeline's tight.
[04:32] Sophie: Okay that's doable — we'll prioritize a 'fast lane' checklist.
[04:36] [00:05:00] Diego: Technical follow-up: on the orchestration side, do you control the node image and are you running a custom fleet manager? How do you expect to consume Redwood artifacts?
[04:46] Samir: We manage node images via our fleet controller — it's based on k8s + Nomad hybrid. We can run the Redwood operator inside our clusters or run a thin shim that proxies to Redwood-managed endpoints. Ideally, we'd prefer an operator-based model for better observability.
[04:59] Diego: Operator approach makes sense if you need fine-grained metrics. We emit Prometheus metrics, traces (OpenTelemetry), and structured events. We also support a lightweight sidecar for legacy fleets that can't run the operator.
[05:12] Jade: Ok on metrics — can we get token-level cost attribution? We want per-customer and per-workload reporting.
[05:18] Sophie: Yes, tagging is supported. You can pass tenant tags on requests and Redwood will aggregate usage per tag. Partner integrations often map Verdant tenant IDs to our tags, then downstream billing consumes that.
[05:28] [00:10:00] Liam: Security question — SSO and RBAC. Our customers expect SAML and enterprise SSO. How do you integrate?
[05:35] Anika: We support SAML 2.0 and OIDC. For partner-managed offerings, SSO can be federated so your customers use their own IdP. RBAC is role-based and maps to API keys and routes; audit events tie actions to identities.
[05:46] Priya: On the commercial side, what's the partner revenue split and are there minimums?
[05:52] Sophie: That varies by channel and scale. We have a standard referral model for modest volume and a rev-share program for committed capacity. Minimums depend on reserved capacity and SLAs. I'll loop in our partnerships legal to send a term sheet.
[06:03] [00:15:00] Samir: A couple of integration nitty-gritty — do you support GPU-specific selectors? For example we want to pin workloads to AIGX-32 or equivalent.
[06:12] Diego: We surface hardware selectors and labels. You can request GPU family, vRAM minimums, and specify MIG slice sizes. The scheduler will try to satisfy the constraints; fallback behavior is configurable in rollout policies.
[06:24] Jade: Do you have any pre-built model marketplace listing templates (docs, banners, sample pricing) we can reuse?
[06:30] Anika: Yes, there's a partner kit: listing templates, sample pricing bands, marketing blurbs. We'll share the kit; it speeds up onboarding.
[06:36] [00:20:00] Priya: Let's talk about SLA and regional uptime — our customers want a 99.9% SLA for inference endpoints. Does Redwood offer that for partner-hosted marketplace endpoints?
[06:46] Sophie: For hosted endpoints on Redwood Dedicated we have SLA options; for partner-managed/private stacks, SLA is a joint responsibility. We can commit to SRE runbooks and escalation paths; official SLA depends on the contract and reserved capacity.
[06:56] Liam: On deployment workflow, can you support canary rollouts and automatic fallback to smaller models when capacity constrained?
[07:02] Diego: Yes — rollout policies support canary percentages, A/B routing, and automatic fallback to compatible variants (e.g., smaller model or quantized variant) when thresholds are exceeded. You can set latency or error-based triggers.
[07:18] Priya: For the pilot customers, two will require on-prem connectors — how heavy is the on-prem package to install? Could your customers run it without deep Redwood involvement?
[07:28] Sophie: We provide a packaged installer and orchestration playbooks. For most customers with an experienced infra team it's straightforward; for regulated setups we often do an initial onboarding engagement to validate HSMs, networking, and compliance.
[07:39] Samir: Can we get a list of sample playbooks? Firewall rules, peering steps, IAM roles, etc.
[07:44] Diego: We'll attach a runbook and a sample terraform module. Action: Diego will drop infra diagram + runbook link.
[07:51] [00:30:00] Jade: Something that could be a blocker: how do you handle model provenance and IP? Our OEM partners may want contract language that limits model redistribution.
[07:59] Anika: Model licensing and provenance are handled per-listing. You can choose to expose a hosted model as 'managed' where Redwood handles inference but doesn't allow model download, or enable private model sync for customers who need a local copy. Licensing obligations are included in the partner agreement.
[08:14] Liam: Does Redwood run governance checks — like model card, evals, and safety filters — that we can tap into?
[08:20] Diego: Yes, we surface model cards, evaluation reports, and safety filters as part of onboarding. We can attach evaluations to listings and fail gating if metrics don't pass your thresholds.
[08:30] [00:40:00] Priya: To align on timeline — if we start work next week, what's a realistic earliest pilot?
[08:36] Sophie: Given your late Q4 target, we can aim for a lightweight pilot in ~8 weeks if we prioritize the EU customer and reuse an existing model bundle. That would require Verdant to assign a tech lead and approve the network and legal templates quickly.
[08:51] Samir: We can spin up a team — I'll be lead and can allocate two SREs.
[08:55] Sophie: Excellent. I'll prepare a 'fast lane' checklist and a proposed schedule.
[09:00] Jade: Any red flags around shared tenancy and noisy neighbor risks?
[09:05] Diego: We mitigate with per-tenant quotas, per-queue isolation, and autoscaling. For strict isolation we recommend dedicated pools per customer. There's a cost tradeoff but it's available.
[09:17] Liam: What's the typical uplift for dedicated pools?
[09:20] Sophie: Depends on utilization and reservation; typical uplift is 10–30% higher than fully-shared cost but gives predictable performance. We'll model numbers for your expected load.
[09:31] [00:50:00] Priya: Okay sounds like good alignment. Let's recap next steps and owners.
[09:36] Sophie: Recap — Redwood to share integration spec, terraform module, infra runbook, and sample perf profiles (Diego). Verdant to share list of pilot customers and technical contacts (Samir/Priya). Legal intro (Sophie) for partner terms. We'll schedule the SE deep dive week of Oct 11.
[09:54] Priya: That's it — thanks all. We'll look out for the docs.
[10:00] Sophie: Thanks everyone, talk soon.

End of transcript.
